claim.text: On the frozen 16-state R1T projected-Simon testbed, a time-ordered noisy action of the non-abelian regular group Z4 semidirect Z4 (inversion action) can alter sector-resolved and global Simon leakage in an order-sensitive way that is absent in the capacity-matched abelian Z4 x Z4 control under the same generator/noise schedule.
claim.scope: Finite exact statevector experiment on 16 amplitudes. Tests representation/order sensitivity under a regular permutation action and time-dependent stochastic generator perturbations; no hardware, asymptotic, biological, manifold, or quantum-speedup claim.
assumptions: non-abelian group presentation a^4=b^4=e and b a b^-1=a^-1
both groups act by left-regular permutations on the same 16 computational-basis labels
the same projected Simon states and the same coherent four-cell partitions from R1T are used
noise schedules are generated before metrics are evaluated and reused identically for non-abelian and abelian controls
time reversal means reversing the exact realized noisy generator word, not resampling noise
forbidden_promotions: no claim that non-abelian symmetry is intrinsically better
no claim of noise robustness unless a matched metric improves under preregistered comparison
no claim about general Z_l semidirect Z_m families from this single Z4 semidirect Z4 instance
no claim that permutation noise models physical device noise

specification.intended_object: For group coordinates (i,j) in Z4 x Z4, compare abelian product (i,j)(k,l)=(i+k,j+l) mod 4 with non-abelian semidirect product (i,j)(k,l)=(i+(-1)^j k,j+l) mod 4. Their left-regular actions induce permutations on 16 projected amplitudes. A time-dependent noisy word w_eta(t) over generators a,b,a^-1,b^-1 is applied stepwise to the projected state and partition labels, then R1T Walsh/interference metrics are evaluated after each step.
invariants: both multiplication laws satisfy identity and inverse checks on all 16 elements
every regular action is a permutation of 0..15
same realized noisy word and same initial state/partition are used across matched group controls
forward and reversed realized words contain identical generator multisets
R1T interference closure remains <=1e-12 after every permutation action
known_answer_cases: zero-noise identity schedule leaves all R1T metrics unchanged
in the abelian control, any forward/reversed words with identical generator multiset produce identical endpoint permutation and endpoint metrics
the non-abelian commutator word a b a^-1 b^-1 is non-identity while the abelian counterpart is identity

implementation.commit: implementation must descend from this preregistration commit
implementation.representation: 16 group elements encoded lexicographically as label 4*j+i; exact left-regular permutation representation

metric.name: time_ordered_group_noise_effect_region
equivalence_attacks: abelian Z4 x Z4 with identical realized word
generator-name relabelling a<->b with matched counts
conjugated non-abelian representation by a fixed random basis permutation

black_box: endpoint permutation from iterative action equals direct product element regular action
metamorphic: conjugated representation preserves relabelled physical predictions
fuzzing: 8 projection seeds x 8 noise seeds x 3 noise profiles
historical: R1T field-vs-random result requires matched structural controls and forbids attributing effects to labels alone

matched_baselines: ABELIAN: Z4 x Z4 regular action with same noisy word
CONJUGATED: non-abelian representation conjugated by fixed label permutation
negative_controls: commutator word must vanish in abelian control and remain nontrivial in non-abelian group
controls.compute_parity: same number of permutation applications, Walsh transforms, states, partitions, and time points
controls.parameter_parity: same generator alphabet and word length
controls.sampling_parity: same projection seeds, noise seeds, and realized words
controls.data_access_parity: same initial projected wavefunction and partition

preregistration.prediction: P1 abelian forward/reverse endpoint metric defect <=1e-12 for every run. P2 non-abelian forward/reverse endpoint permutation differs for at least 75% of nontrivial noisy words and endpoint metric defect is >1e-8 for at least one preregistered metric in at least 50% of nondegenerate runs. P3 zero-noise identity leaves metrics unchanged <=1e-12. P4 conjugating the representation and consistently relabelling state/partition leaves metrics unchanged <=1e-12. P5 interference closure remains <=1e-12 at all time points.
preregistration.primary_metric: paired forward-vs-reverse endpoint defect vector: (permutation_disagreement, global_forbidden_mass_defect, sector_forbidden_mass_defect, offdiag_forbidden_defect), compared non-abelian versus abelian
preregistration.uncertainty_method: exact finite permutations plus deterministic seeded noise; report every row and aggregate proportions over 8x8x3 matched cells
preregistration.kill_condition: Retire the non-abelian order-sensitivity interpretation if the abelian forward/reverse endpoint differs above 1e-12, if conjugation changes consistently relabelled metrics above 1e-12, if interference closure exceeds 1e-12, or if non-abelian endpoint permutation differs but no preregistered wavefunction metric differs above 1e-8 in at least 50% of nondegenerate runs.
preregistration.stop_condition: Stop after the four controls, three fixed noise profiles, 8 projection seeds, 8 noise seeds, and time-series/end-point metrics are recorded. No adiabatic, sheaf, holoportation, continuous Lie, or larger Z_l semidirect Z_m sweep inside R1U.
preregistration.promotion_rule: H -> M only for the bounded statement that order-sensitive non-abelian regular actions under the declared time-dependent noise produce a reproducible effect on these projected-partition metrics beyond matched abelian/relabelled controls. Any stronger geometric interpretation remains H/S.
